subject: Syslog onramp + trace bridge onboarding for ACME Health
messages:
From: Alex Rivas <alex.rivas@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: SysOps Team <sysops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: onboarding syslog + trace hooks into Redwood Private

Hi Marissa,

We're kicking off the telemetry onboarding for our Redwood Private deployment in the ACME Health VPC. Goal: ship syslog (RFC5424) and OTLP trace exports into your private forwarder without exposing PHI, and make sure our SIEM mappings land into splunk index:acme_prod_ingest.

Can your team confirm the recommended network pattern (reverse proxy vs. customer-initiated forwarder), required firewall/NAT ports, and the evidence checklist for SOC2 audit? I'll attach a sample syslog config.

Thanks,
Alex Rivas
Senior Platform Engineer
ACME Health

Attachments: acme_syslog_config_sample.conf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Rivas <alex.rivas@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding syslog + trace hooks into Redwood Private

Alex — thanks for the config and the clear ask. Looping in Ben (on-prem observability) and Kim (security) so we can validate the network pattern and audit evidence.

High-level answers up front:
- Two supported patterns: outbound customer-initiated (preferred for locked-down environments) or inbound well-scoped TLS egress to a customer-managed proxy in their VPC.
- Ports: 6514 (syslog TLS) recommended; 4317/4318 for OTLP. If you must use 514/UDP we require a collector inside the VPC.
- Evidence we typically provide: transport config snippets, TLS cert thumbprints, routing table / peering screenshots, and a signed forwarder manifest.

Ben/Kim: can you propose a minimal implementation playbook (1-2 page) for ACME and call out any controls that would block SOC2?

—Marissa
Product Solutions (Redwood)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Rivas <alex.rivas@acmehealth.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding syslog + trace hooks into Redwood Private

Marissa / Alex — draft plan below. I'll attach the tracehook-spec and a short checklist.

1) Pattern: Customer-initiated outbound to our private forwarder (TLS mutual-auth) inside their VPC. This requires a small collector (rsyslog/syslog-ng or Fluent Bit) that you run in ACME subnets. Advantages: no inbound firewall openings to ACME, easier for air-gapped policies.

2) Network config: allow outbound TCP 6514 and TCP 443 from the collector to the Redwood forwarder ELB. For OTLP traces, allow 4317/4318 outbound to our OTLP endpoint. If ACME wants to terminate TLS to a proxy, we can accept PEM bundles via our handoff flow.

3) SIEM mapping: we will map RFC5424 pri and structured data into fields: syslog_severity, host_env, application_id. For Splunk HEC ingestion we'll provide a signed mapping file and example event->index routing.

4) Trace hooks: include X-Trace-Id and sampling flags in the forwarder; we'll preserve headers into OTLP attributes. We'll validate via trace sampler tests (small load tests) before go-live.

5) Audit evidence: we provide the tracehook-spec.md, TLS cert fingerprints, a runbook snippet, and the evidence_manifest.zip (signed by both parties).

Open items for ACME:
- Which subnet(s) will the collector run in?
- Do you require explicit IP allowlist or will hostname/ALB TLS + mTLS be sufficient?

Sean: can you add the minimal infra firewall diagram / NAT rules?

—Ben
On-Prem Observability, Redwood

Attachments: tracehook-spec.md, evidence_manifest.zip

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Alex Rivas <alex.rivas@acmehealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 14:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding syslog + trace hooks into Redwood Private

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick responses. From a security/compliance perspective we need to confirm a few controls before we move to a formal evidence bundle: 

- Data minimization: confirm only non-PHI fields are forwarded to Redwood. If PHI must be forwarded, we need a separate DPA and field-level redaction.
- Key management: mTLS key material must be HSM-backed on Redwood side if ACME requests key escrow.
- Access logs: ACME needs audit logs showing which Redwood operator accessed telemetry config or evidence artifacts (we provide token-level tracing but ask if ACME has extra requirements).
- Retention: confirm retention windows for raw logs vs parsed events.

Please respond to the bullets and paste a sample sanitized syslog event (one-line) for us to test parsing. We'll then produce the SOC2 evidence manifest.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security Operations, Redwood

From: Alex Rivas <alex.rivas@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: SysOps Team <sysops@acmehealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2026 16:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding syslog + trace hooks into Redwood Private

Thanks all — quick answers and a sanitized sample below.

- Data minimization: ACME will redact PHI at the collector (we run a lua filter in Fluent Bit). Only environment, service, severity, timestamp, and correlation ids will be forwarded. PHI fields will be dropped.
- Key mgmt: ACME will supply a client cert signed by our org CA for mTLS; Redwood can present its cert chain. We do not require Redwood HSM for this phase.
- Access logs: we will need operator access logs for audit; our compliance team will review the format you provide.
- Retention: raw syslog retained 30 days in ACME; parsed events retained 365 days on Redwood (we will need this in writing).

Sanitized syslog sample (RFC5424):
<34>1 2026-12-09T16:45:12Z acme-svc1 acme.payment 1234 - [acme@32473 env=prod service=payments transaction=xxxxxx] "PAYMENT processed, status=OK"

Next steps: Ben/Marissa — once you confirm the inbound/outbound pattern and send the runbook + firewall diagram, we'll schedule a small validation window (30 minutes) next week to pump 500 events/min and confirm parsing and traces.

—Alex
